actions: Read sanitized root control and neuroscience-only role config at frozen SHA, rechecked SHA-only head before semantic work, and preserved CLEAN isolation.
Retried read-only public-source recovery context; PLOS SPLiT binary source remained unavailable through safe transport, so no source-exact S8/S11/S12 claim was made.

Ran held-out nonlinear synthetic controls for event-sparse dormant-memory admission versus naive lost-component storage across PAST/GROUSE-like and Oja-like trackers under moderate and severe delayed/sparse feedback.
Added a tracker-shared sticky latent-cause-style posterior screen using disjoint calibration streams and compared it with the current standardized CUSUM release control.

Reviewed Lu et al. 2024 LCNet public article/code as related public evidence for predictive-likelihood plus sticky-prior latent-cause inference, without treating the synthetic detector as an LCNet reproduction.
Wrote and read back the immutable neuroscience delta and advanced LATEST with CAS.
result_summary: Event-sparse admission reduced false-admission churn by roughly 82-86% but also missed most true returns and produced no resolved task-loss gain. A coarse sticky latent-cause screen improved persistent-switch detection under 40-step delay/25% labels from 12.5% for the current CUSUM control to 41.7% PAST-like and 37.5% Oja-like, with modestly more false releases and long latency. The single reconstruction-residual unsupervised channel was weak.
exact_next_action: Retry PLOS Figshare Code.zip read-only recovery. Replace the coarse binned HMM with a source-derived predictive-likelihood latent-cause/run-length posterior using an explicit temporal-autocorrelation prior and richer unsupervised covariance/subspace-change likelihood. Lock parameters on disjoint calibration environments, test hazard transfer across tracker families and altered switch/silence statistics, then use the posterior jointly for dormant-memory promotion and release. Report task loss, bank churn, true/false admission/release, latency and posterior calibration; keep SPLiT conclusions bounded until S1 code is recovered.
